title: Constructible sheaves over a discrete Noetherian ring form a weak Serre subcategory
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], regarded as discrete. On the small étale or small pro-étale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], use sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $\underline R$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Call a sheaf constructible if, for every affine open $U\subseteq X$, there is a finite partition $U=\coprod_{a<n} Z_a$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification], [def-weil-constructible-subset], with immersion maps $Z_a\to U$, such that the inverse-image restriction to each $Z_a$ (the module inverse image along $Z_a\to U\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]) is locally constant with finitely presented $R$-module values: locally on the site of $Z_a$, as module sheaves on the localized sites, it is isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finitely presented $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-locally-constant-module-sheaf], [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. On either site the constructible sheaves contain zero and are closed under kernels and cokernels of morphisms between constructible sheaves, and under extensions: if $0\to F\to E\to G\to0$ is exact and $F,G$ are constructible, then $E$ is constructible. In other words they form a weak Serre subcategory, with the displayed closure properties as its meaning. No finiteness of the underlying set of $R$ and no invertibility on $X$ is assumed.

proof.text: First compare the two finiteness conventions used below. A finitely presented R-module is finitely generated: the images of the standard basis of R^n in a finite presentation generate it. Conversely, since R is Noetherian, every finitely generated R-module is finitely presented by the cited Noetherian finite-module theorem. Thus locally constant sheaves with finitely presented values are exactly locally constant sheaves of finite type, on either site.

source.place: Tag 00IK, lemma-Noetherian-basic, first assertion; finite presentation definition

proof.text: For a morphism h:T→S, let L be its set-sheaf inverse image. The étale inverse-image statement supplies the finite-limit-preserving left adjoint; the pro-étale construction supplies the geometric morphism arising from the covering-preserving base-change functor. The general left-exact-site theorem gives preservation of all colimits as well. Consequently L preserves constant sheaves: the constant sheaf with set value A is the coproduct of A copies of the terminal sheaf (both have maps to H given by A-indexed families of global sections), and L preserves this coproduct and the terminal sheaf. These identifications are natural in A; applying them to addition, multiplication and the module action gives L(underline R_S)≅underline R_T and L(underline M_S)≅underline M_T as ring and module sheaves, for every R-module M. There is no finiteness restriction on R or M.

Use the coefficient identification of step 2 to equip LF with its R-module structure, by applying L to the action and using preservation of products. This agrees with the module inverse image of the site definitions: on the pro-étale site the structure map $c^f_R$ and the step-2 isomorphism are maps out of the constant sheaf $L(\underline R_S)$, and both correspond under the adjunction to the family $a\mapsto$ (constant section $a$ of $\underline R_T$), so they coincide; tensoring along this isomorphism changes nothing. Inverse image on abelian sheaves is exact by the cited site-pullback theorem. Kernels and cokernels of module sheaves have the underlying abelian kernels and cokernels (sectionwise kernels and sheafified sectionwise cokernels). Therefore this module inverse image preserves kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences. In particular this holds for every stratum immersion on either site; a closed stratum is treated by inverse image of topoi, not by identifying its site with a slice of the ambient site.

source.place: Tag 04JC, lemma-flat-pullback-exact, first assertion; Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian

proof.text: For every affine open U⊆X, choose finite partitions of U witnessing constructibility of F|U and G|U, and apply the common-refinement node to U. Its strata are the fibre products Z_k×_U W_l, with constructible locally closed images, and map to each original stratum. Pull back a trivializing covering of F on Z_k to Z_k×_U W_l, and a trivializing covering of G on W_l to the same fibre product. These are coverings by the cited étale-covering base-change theorem for the étale site, and by the covering-preserving base-change functor of the pro-étale inverse-image construction in step 2 for the pro-étale site. On a member $V'=Z_k\times_U W_l\times_{Z_k}V$ of the pulled-back covering, the localization-exchange theorem gives $(h^{-1}\mathcal F_k)|_{V'}\cong h_V^{-1}(\mathcal F_k|_V)$ for the localized morphism $h_V$, where $h$ is the projection to $Z_k$ and $\mathcal F_k$ the restriction of $F$ to $Z_k$; since $\mathcal F_k|_V$ is constant, step 2 (whose argument applies to $h_V$, a morphism of sites given by a covering- and finite-limit-preserving functor) shows these restrictions are the same constant module sheaves. The same holds for $G$. Thus F|U and G|U are locally constant with finitely presented values on each common stratum. The identification of iterated inverse image with inverse image of the composite is the adjoint-compatible isomorphism in the cited site-composition theorem; the base-change functors compose through the canonical fibre-product isomorphism. Since this holds for every affine U, the resulting kernels, cokernels, and extensions satisfy the affine-local constructibility definition.

source.place: Tag 03RZ, lemma-constructible-abelian, common finite partition in the proof of (3), applied on each affine open U; site composition: sites.tex Tag 03CB, lemma-composition-morphisms-sites

proof.text: Apply step 3 to restrict the kernel, cokernel, or short exact sequence to each common stratum. The two known sheaves there are locally constant of finite type by steps 1 and 4. Apply the cited local weak-Serre theorem to that stratum’s small site and the same commutative Noetherian ring R: its conclusion gives locally constant finite-type kernels and cokernels, or a locally constant finite-type middle term. The small-site hypothesis is satisfied by taking the chosen small skeletons in a sufficiently large universe, as in the site conventions; the theorem does not require points or finiteness of the set R. Step 1 converts the resulting module values back to finitely presented values. Hence the finite common stratification witnesses constructibility of the required sheaf.

For every affine open U⊆X, the zero sheaf restricted to U is constant with value the zero R-module, which has the finite presentation R^0→R^0→0→0. The identity stratum U→U therefore witnesses its constructibility; when U is empty the empty stratification also suffices. Steps 4 and 5 prove kernels, cokernels and extensions on every affine open for either choice of site, which together with zero are precisely the closure conditions stated in the item.
